To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the heptavalen pneumococcal vaccine was associated with a decrease in the carriage of PCV7-serotype erythromycin- and penicillin-resistant pneumococcal isolates.
the heptavalant pneumococcal vaccine (PCV) does not affect the carriage of erytromycin-resistant S.pneumoniae, except for the vaccine types.
the widespread immunization of the day-care center attendees with PCV7 has not led to a significant decrease in the carriage of antimicrobial-resistant pneumococcal strains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the complex interaction of PCV7 immunizations and antimicrobials on the nasopharylgeal colonization with eryhromycin-resistant pneumoocci.
the interaction of PCV7 and antimicrobial agents on pneumococcal carriage in day-care centers, which are a reservoir of pneumococcal colonization.
the interaction of the hepta-valent pneumococci conjugate vaccine (PVC7) and individual antibiotics on the nasoph-aryngeal carriage in children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PCV7 immunized children are less likely to be carriers of erythromycinsusceptible pneumococci than unvaccinated children.
the pneumococcal vaccine is effective in reducing the carriage of pneumococci but not the overall carriage of erythryomycin-resistant pneumococcus.
the pneumococcal vaccination program has not been able to reduce the carriage of erythropoenic-resistant pneumococcal strains in children.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

PCV7 immunizations are effective in decreasing the carriage of erythropoietic-resistant S. pneumonia serotypes, but not of nonvaccine serotypes, and that the use of macrolides has a significant correlation with the carriage with erythromyicin resistant pneumococci.
the heptavalen pneumococcal vaccine has not been able to reduce the prevalence of erythromycine-resistant pneumococcal strains, but it seems that it can prevent their spread.
PCV7 immunizations, particularly when administered early in life, can reduce the nasopharynx carriage of pneumococcal serotypes that are included in the vaccine.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of antimicrobials in the day-care center attendees, especially macrolides, should be limited to those cases in which they are absolutely necessary, as they may cause the dissemination of resistant pneumococci.

the heptavalant pneumococcal vaccine does not protect against the acquisition of macrolide-resistant pneumococcal strains, particularly those that are not included in the vaccine, and that the widespread use of macrolides is associated with the dissemination of macrolide resistance in pneumococci.
PCV7 vaccination is a powerful tool to decrease the carriage of erythro-mycin-resistant S. pneumoniae serotypes.
